chunks: And it is narrated: that Abū Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, stood by the Kaʿbah and said: I am Jundab ibn al-Sakan. Then the people gathered around him, and he said: If one of you intended a journey, he would take for it provisions that would set him right for his journey. So take provisions for the journey of the Day of Resurrection. Do you not desire therein that which will set you right?

Then a man stood up to him and said: Guide us. He said: Fast on an intensely hot day for the Resurrection; perform a hajj for the tremendous matters; and pray two rakʿahs in the darkness of the night for the loneliness of the graves; a good word that you speak, and an evil word from which you remain silent; or charity from you to a needy person—perhaps by it, O poor one, you may be saved from a difficult day.

Make the world into two dirhams: one dirham that you spend on your dependents, and one dirham that you send ahead for your Hereafter. The third harms and does not benefit, so do not desire it. Make the world into two words: a word in seeking the halal, and a word for the Hereafter. The third harms and does not benefit, so do not desire it.
Then he said: The worry of a day I will not reach has slain me.

key_terms.الزَّادِ: provisions prepared for a journey, here meaning deeds stored for the Hereafter
key_terms.حُجَّ: perform hajj, the pilgrimage to the Sacred House
key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ: charity given to a needy person for Allah’s sake
key_terms.صَلِّ: perform salat (prayer), here specifically two rakʿahs at night
key_terms.صُمْ: fast; an act of worship undertaken for divine reward
key_terms.لِآخِرَتِكَ: for your Hereafter, meaning what is sent ahead in righteous deeds
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when people are raised and judged

ai.seo_question: How should a believer prepare for the journey of the Day of Resurrection according to Abū Dharr?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Abū Dharr, رحمه الله, exhorting people to prepare for the afterlife just as they would prepare provisions for a worldly journey. He highlights acts of worship, restraint in speech, charity, lawful earning, and moderation in worldly concerns as means of salvation on the Day of Resurrection.
